rules.statement: A self-service password change must end every other session of the end user and revoke every grant issued under no session, while keeping the current session and the user's consents.
rules.why: NIST SP 800-63B and OWASP ASVS V3.3.3 require ending the sessions an old authenticator authenticated, and ending the current session would sign out the session that proved the change.
rules.check: A password-change handler that returns success without revoking the other sessions and sessionless grants, or that also revokes the current session or the consents.

rules.statement: When terminating several sessions, claim all of them and revoke the grants first, then dispatch each termination notification, so a failed dispatch cannot leave a claimed session's grants active.
rules.why: If a dispatch fails, only the grants of the current session stay active.
rules.check: Code that sends termination notifications in the same loop as the claim or before the grants are revoked.

rules.statement: Before changing a password, verify the current password and require the verified account to be the same account as the authenticated principal's, and report a failure otherwise.
rules.why: A current password that is valid for a different account must not authorize changing this account's password.
rules.check: A password change that verifies the current password by user name but does not compare the verified account id with the principal's account id.

rules.statement: Encode passwords and other secret strings into SecureMemoryPool buffers (NCode.Buffers) rather than ordinary arrays or pooled buffers.
rules.why: The ADR requires both passwords to be held in secure buffers that are cleared when released.
rules.check: Password bytes encoded with Encoding.GetBytes into a new array, or rented from ArrayPool or MemoryPool.Shared.

rules.statement: Register the default implementation of an optional, replaceable seam with TryAdd* (e.g. TryAddSingleton), and have a feature package that provides a real implementation replace it.
rules.why: With TryAdd*, a host or backend package can provide its own implementation and the default (such as one that reports no support) is not registered twice.
rules.check: A default seam implementation registered with AddSingleton/AddScoped, so a host registration is either overridden or duplicated.

rules.statement: Keep a capability that only some backends support, such as a password change, on its own optional interface instead of adding it as a member of a broader required interface.
rules.why: Passwordless or external backends would need to implement a member they cannot answer.
rules.check: A new member added to a widely implemented interface that most implementations would have to stub out or throw from.

rules.statement: Validate a new password against the password policy before verifying the current password, and verify the current password under the per-account limit on failed attempts.
rules.why: Amendments ADR-0236 and ADR-0237 make one policy judge every password, and make every password verification count toward the attempt limit.
rules.check: A password change that skips the policy check, checks the policy only after verifying the current password, or verifies the current password without the failed-attempt limiter.
